Stopped before claim. The required S2 kernel (#2627) is not on `upstream/main` `744c0847b`.

- `Cargo.toml` and `crates/` have no `camcraft-gpu` crate on `upstream/main`.
- `crates/ui/src/trace.rs` still uploads CPU cut buffers through `TracePass::write_cut` and `TracePass::write_cut_patch`.
- Blocker #2611 is closed (PR #2644).
- Blocker #2627 remains open with no claim, no branch, and no open PR.
- Issue #2620 (which blocks #2627) remains open and `claimed` on branch `issue/2620-gpu-compute-seam`, with no open PR to stack on.
- Open PR #2714 touches `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs` and `crates/app/src/stock_view.rs`, and does not provide S2.

S3 (#2629) requires the S2 kernel (#2627) and `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` (#2620). Adding S2 and `camcraft-gpu` here exceeds the scope of #2629.
This run made no claim, branch, worktree, code change, or test run.

<!-- deps: 2627 -->
Blocked: waits on #2627 (this issue's text says it depends on that work, which is still open). The label comes off automatically when they close.

The maintainer reported in chat on 2026-11-22: "bug; performance; P2; the stock simulation; is extremly slow. This was supposed to be calculated on the GPU as a shader, it doesnt seem to be the case.." The report is #3336.

This issue is part of the fix of #3336. Its priority changes from P4 to P2, and its type from enhancement to bug. The order of the GPU path stays: #2620, then #2627, then #2629.

Facts for S3 from the S2 kernel (PR #3532, #2627). This comment records them. It does not fix them.

- The shared device of `camcraft-gpu` (`shared_device`) is not the render device of the UI. The cut buffer `scene.cut` is made on the render device (`crates/ui/src/trace.rs:197-203`). The S3 caller has two options:
  - make its own `CutKernel::new(render_device)` and run `CutKernel::run` on the render device and queue;
  - or use `cut_or_cpu` on the shared device and upload the result with `write_cut` (a read-back and an upload).
- The kernel writes u32 ordered keys during the cut (`atomicMax`). The third pass `cs_decode` turns each key into the bits of its f32 in the same buffer. After the pass, `trace.wgsl` can read the buffer as `array<f32>`, in the `pack_cut` layout. A kernel that writes into `scene.cut` directly needs `STORAGE` usage on that buffer (it has it) and a bind group that the kernel owns.
- The input is plain numbers. `camcraft_sim::stock_sim::twin_items` gives `TwinItem { tile, base, lo, hi }`; S3 maps it to `camcraft_gpu::CutItem` field by field.
- `CutKernel::run` blocks for at most `CUT_WAIT` (10 s). S3 must call it off the UI thread.
- The render device has no `on_uncaptured_error` handler that this kernel installs. The kernel uses error scopes on the calling thread.

Preconditions for this slice (S3), from the review of PR #3532 (the kernel of #2627):

1. The kernel was run on the software adapter only. On a hardware adapter the WGSL division and `sqrt` are not always correctly rounded, and a compiler can fuse multiply and add. The estimate is that the error stays under half of the claim margin (4.9e-5). This is not proven. Prove the parity on a hardware adapter before something other than the display reads the buffer.
2. `adapter.rs:78` takes the software adapter first. In the product the shared device is then WARP, which runs on the CPU. This slice must use the render device or a hardware adapter.
3. `cut_or_cpu` always takes the GPU when one exists. The ball case is slower on the GPU for a small batch (11.9 ms against 1.1 ms on the fixture). Choose the path by batch size and adapter type, from timings measured on hardware.
Unblocked: #2627 closed. The issue is free to pick.

claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus, for qsmits) · 2026-11-22T22:41Z · branch qsmits:issue/2629-gpu-playback-cut · plan: run the S2 cut kernel on the render device off the UI thread, write scene.cut directly, CPU playback on any error or when CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off

Escalation: this work is larger than `effort:high`. The claim of issue-worker-high (for qsmits) is released. No code was written. The branch `issue/2629-gpu-playback-cut` has no commits and is not pushed.

A collaborator must change the label to `effort:max`. A contributor cannot set labels.

## What I learned (main `e6952a847`)

The S2 kernel cannot replace the playback cut as it is. These are the gaps:

1. **The kernel cuts from zero.** `CutKernel::submit` (`crates/gpu/src/cut_gpu.rs:182-229`) runs `cs_fill`, then `cs_cut`, then `cs_decode` into a new key buffer, and `run` reads the result back. `twin_cut` and `cut_cpu` also start from the `-4 cap` floor. Playback needs an incremental cut: a keyframe buffer plus the next moves. After `cs_decode`, the buffer holds f32 bits, not ordered keys. An incremental cut needs a new kernel mode (no fill, an encode pass or a persistent key buffer) and a new entry that writes into a caller buffer (`scene.cut`) with no read-back. That is a change to the kernel and its parity proof.
2. **The twin covers only part of a playback.** `twin_work` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cut_twin_work.rs:60-170`) refuses arcs, tilted axes, zero-length moves and all tools except the ball and the flat end mill. The CPU playback (`FieldPlay::cut`, `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs:397`) cuts all these kinds (undercut, lathe, rotary, drill). A session with one refused operation needs a merge law of CPU cuts and GPU cuts in one layer. The max law permits it, but the design is open.
3. **The playback state lives in the app worker.** `stock_play_worker.rs:341-406` owns `FieldPlay`, the checkpoints, the fractional move (`seek_to(k, f)`), the precalc budget and the patch chain. The UI (`trace/eye.rs:258`) gets only packed `FieldView` frames. For a real speedup the worker must skip the CPU cut on the GPU path and send the move work to the UI instead. Then a GPU fault must rebuild the CPU field from a checkpoint. This changes the protocol between `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`, in two files that are already over 400 lines (434 and 406).
4. **Keyframes in VRAM.** The issue asks for keyframes as GPU buffer copies within a VRAM budget, and a seek from the nearest keyframe. No such store exists. Its budget and its eviction law are new design.
5. **The threshold has no data.** Precondition 3 asks for a choice by batch size and adapter type from hardware timings. The only numbers are the fixture numbers in the review of PR #3532.

A smaller variant is possible: run `CutKernel::run` on the render device for each frame and call `write_cut`. This variant keeps the CPU cut in the worker, so the playback is not faster. It does not meet "Done means" or the goal of #3336.

## Recommended split

- S3a (`effort:max`): an incremental kernel mode that cuts into a caller buffer, with the parity test against `cut_cpu` on the same base layer.
- S3b (`effort:max`): the worker protocol. The worker sends twin work for each frame on the GPU path and keeps CPU checkpoints for the fallback and the refused operations.
- S3c (`effort:high`): the UI side in `trace/`. It dispatches the work off the UI thread on the render device, keeps the keyframe store, and falls back to the CPU frames on any error.

Held work: none. The claim is released.
